native_notes.text:
As a reminder, do your workout comments going forward like this:

1. Workout Readiness - (e.g. 6/10; couldn't fall asleep bc of stress)
2. Workout Execution - (e.g. 5/10; skipped last set after going too hard in the first set)
3. Nutrition - (e.g. 5/10; didn't eat during my hard 2 hour interval ride, but did eat before and after)
4. Misc - (e.g. lower back acting up again)

1-3: Rate out of 10 (10 is the best); add details if possible; e.g., "I ate two 50g carbohydrate bars" or "Felt sluggish to start" etc.
Misc: Have at it, or don't.
native_notes.title: How To Comment On Workouts

native_notes.text:
Week 1 of 4. Testing week: two assessments, everything else easy. I build the rest of the plan from what you do here.

This block: Re-entry after a lapsed season. Rebuild visible, unmissable calendar structure and training frequency across bike/run/MTB/strength before adding duration or intensity. FTP re-anchored at 300W (coach-confirmed 2026-08-23, "300 is about right") -- bike structure may run %FTP. No A-race; consistency is the trained adaptation.

This week sets the numbers. Do not train through the tests; show up fresh.
native_notes.title: Week 1: Testing

native_notes.text:
Tell me:
1. What went well and why?
2. What went badly and why?
3. ONE thing you can DO next week that's:
 a) In your control
 b) Not too big of a lift
 c) Impactful

Please complete this at the end of every week and put your answers in the comments on this note. It will greatly improve you as an athlete and help me coach you better.
native_notes.title: Week Self Review - 3 Qs

native_notes.text:
Week 2 of 4. Base. Nothing flashy; I want steady work and the point is accumulation.

Ronnestad 30-15 Tuesday. The short recoveries are the trick: you never fully recover, so the oxygen system stays pinned without the legs blowing up.

Cadence HC Thursday: power stays flat, the gear changes. Low rungs load the legs, high rungs teach them to spin. Watch the knees on the low stuff.

Rest days count. Strava does not.

Watch the easy days. If they creep up in pace, the hard days will start falling short.
native_notes.title: Week 2: Base

native_notes.text: Legs heavy today is the load landing, not a warning sign.
native_notes.title: Week 2: Midweek

native_notes.text: Fuel the long ride from hour zero, not when you get hungry.

native_notes.text:
Week 3 of 4. Last load week of this block. I want the key sessions done properly; a reset follows.

Ronnestad 30-15 Tuesday is the hardest thing this week. Start the first rep at the number, not above it, and let the set get hard on its own.

Descending-Cadence Ladder Wednesday is skill work, not fitness work. Smooth circles at every cadence; the rpm targets are in the workout.

Sleep is the variable you control. Seven hours minimum this week, more after the hard days.
native_notes.title: Week 3: Base

native_notes.text: If today feels flat, that is the last two hard days still in your legs. Normal.
native_notes.title: Week 3: Midweek

native_notes.text: Bottles mixed and food counted before you roll out for the long one.

native_notes.text:
Week 4 of 4. Recovery week, and I mean it: the last block gets absorbed now, not later.

Tune-Up Tuesday: short, sharp, and done before you feel like you have started. The point is to wake the legs, not test them.

Fatigue should drop noticeably by Thursday. If it does not, say so before the weekend.

workouts.description:
FUEL:
Normal meal ~2h before. One bottle, 40-50g carbs. Done.

12m progressive warmup
-
5m RPE 6/10
-
5m RPE 2
-
5m RPE 8-10. Go as hard as you can for 5 minutes. Note here, start out firm but hard for the first 2 minutes and then adjust your effort up or down.
-
5m RPE 2
-
20m ALL OUT. Start the effort conservatively at about an 8/10 RPE - 20 minutes is a LONG time.
-
You'll want the terrain to be unbroken flat or slightly uphill - you don't want to get caught at a stop light or intersection in the middle of your effort.
-
10m easy spin to cool down.

workouts.description:
Heat Acclimation Protocol — level 1

WARM-UP:
-10min ramp 50%->65% FTP (RPE 2-3)

MAIN SET:
-50min @ 63%-73% FTP (Z2, RPE 2-3, 85-95rpm)

COOL-DOWN:
-10min spin-down 70%->50% FTP (RPE 2-3)

HOW TO RIDE IT:
-Easy and conversational the whole way.

FUEL:
-40-60g carbs/hr.

HEAT PROTOCOL: ~60min at the prescribed easy zone with reduced cooling — skip the fan, add a layer, or ride the hottest part of the day. Hydrate aggressively before and during; sip past thirst. Stop if dizzy, nauseous, or confused — cool down and end the session rather than push through.

workouts.description:

-15-20min progressing Z1->Z2

-Torque rises every rung because power stays flat as rpm drops

EXECUTION:

NUTRITION:
-40-70g carbs/hr.

HYDRATION:
-500-750ml/hr.

workouts.title: Rest Day

workouts.description:
FUEL:
Normal meal ~2h before. One bottle, 40-50g carbs. Done.

MAIN SET:
- 24min @ 65% FTP (Z2, RPE 3)
- 2 x (0:18 @ 140% FTP (Z5+, RPE 8-9) + 2:30 @ 55% FTP (Z2, RPE 3))
- 0:18 @ 140% FTP (Z5+, RPE 8-9)
- 5min @ 50% FTP (Z1, RPE 3)
-Cadence: 95-105rpm on efforts
-Position: Seated, relaxed

PROGRESSION:
-Level 1/6: Introductory - Focus on form and learning the workout pattern
-Short alactic openers -- three brief near-max efforts to wake up neuromuscular firing without creating fatigue

EXECUTION:
-Short sharp efforts to keep the legs remembering speed. Don't dig deep - this should feel like play, not training.
